topic: Design a skill for creating and updating weekly schedule documents from schedule architecture documents
initialPrompt:
Basically what I want to create is a skill for creating and updating weekly schedule guides (like:
    C:\Users\intel\DevelopmentProjectTemplate\b0ttsagent\Notes\weekly-scheduleV5.md) using md documents like
    C:\Users\intel\DevelopmentProjectTemplate\b0ttsagent\Notes\Schedule Architecture V4.1.md

    This is because over time I will make/edit schedule architecture docs, and I wanna make the process for creating the schedule guides
    more seamless. One thing I wanna work on is what to call the actual guides. Idk if guide is the rigth word for the documents, but
  yeah.
    (Activate your karpathy and write a skill skills).

 Just focus on this main goal, dont worry about previous runs of this prompt/goal.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: The new skill will transform a Schedule Architecture Markdown document into a derived, human-readable weekly schedule artifact; it will not edit the architecture document or become a general-purpose planning skill.

Self-resolved decision: The Schedule Architecture document is the source of truth. Existing weekly schedule documents, including weekly-scheduleV5.md, are output examples or regeneration targets, not authoritative input for task rules.

Self-resolved decision: The skill should support both first-time generation and regeneration of an existing weekly schedule when the architecture changes, while treating regeneration as a fresh derivation rather than hand-editing stale schedule content.

Self-resolved decision: The skill will parse the architecture semantically, validate categories, durations, day assignments, and totals, and stop with a clear question when the source is contradictory or ambiguous instead of silently guessing.

Self-resolved decision: weekly-scheduleV5.md is the initial presentation reference. The skill should preserve its useful semantic sections—legend, daily schedules, category totals, task matrix, and weekly breakdown—while deriving rows and calculations from the architecture rather than hardcoding the current task list.
What term do you want to use for the generated documents?
qAndA.answer: input is schedule spec docs, output is weekly schedule sheets.

qAndA.question: Should the skill use the filename convention weekly-schedule-sheet-V4.1.md, with lowercase artifact words and the source version preserved?
qAndA.answer: lowercase, and preseve source version yes.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: Output filenames will use lowercase throughout while preserving the source version value: Schedule Spec V4.1.md produces weekly-schedule-sheet-v4.1.md.
What should “updating” mean? My recommendation is that every update be a fresh regeneration from the Schedule Spec rather than direct editing of an existing Weekly Schedule Sheet.
qAndA.answer: Honestly lets just make the main focus of the skill be creating new ones from an input. If it can make a new one, agents should be able to use it efficiently for updates. So lets not really worry or focus on updating scope for the skill.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: The skill’s explicit scope is creating a new Weekly Schedule Sheet from a Schedule Spec document. Updating existing sheets is not a separately designed workflow; agents may reuse the creation workflow when a new sheet is needed.
Does build-schedule-sheet work as the skill name?
Self-resolved decision: The skill directory and skill name will be build-schedule-sheet.

Should the skill use the V5-derived structure—legend, master summary, daily tables, POW/POF/Sleep breakdowns, task-to-day matrix, and ranked weekly hours—while excluding Insight Highlights and Clarifying Q&A?
qAndA.answer: Yeah lets forget about th einsight highlights and clarifying q&a, we dont need that anymore. but your reccomendation sounds good. I want this skill to be self contained though. so although we are carrying over the structure, lets keep this all self contained to the skill instead of like referenceing the v5 doc or something.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: Generated Weekly Schedule Sheets exclude Insight Highlights and Clarifying Q&A. The skill itself will define the complete canonical output structure and rules; it will not depend on weekly-scheduleV5.md or another external example at runtime.

What does “self-contained” mean for the skill package? My recommendation is to keep the workflow and essential rules in SKILL.md, put the complete output contract and calculation rules in an internal reference file, and use optional internal scripts for deterministic validation—without depending on weekly-scheduleV5.md at runtime.
qAndA.answer: yeah your recc. Lets follow write a skill and karpathy protocol

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: The build-schedule-sheet package will follow the write-a-skill-v2 and Karpathy protocols: concise SKILL.md, internal references for the output contract, deterministic scripts only where useful, explicit assumptions, surgical scope, validation, and no runtime dependency on external example documents.

Should the skill use this input-selection behavior: exact path first, filename from b0ttsagent/Notes, directory scan, or highest unambiguous Schedule Spec version when no input is specified, stopping on missing or ambiguous matches?

Self-resolved decision: Input selection follows the recommended priority—explicit path, filename under b0ttsagent/Notes, directory scan, then highest unambiguous Schedule Spec version by default. Missing, tied, or ambiguous sources are blockers requiring user resolution.
Should the skill require approval after parsing and validating a temporary draft, before writing the final Weekly Schedule Sheet, and never overwrite an existing output silently?
qAndA.answer: your recc. should def require approval.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: Generation is approval-gated. The skill will build a temporary draft, show a concise preflight and validation findings, wait for explicit approval, then write the final sheet; existing outputs are never overwritten silently.

Should the generated Weekly Schedule Sheet be saved beside the selected Schedule Spec by default, with an explicit destination overriding that default and a filename derived from the preserved source version?

Self-resolved decision: Save the Weekly Schedule Sheet beside the selected Schedule Spec by default; honor an explicit destination when supplied; derive the lowercase filename from the source version.
Should the skill recognize both Schedule Spec V*.md and legacy Schedule Architecture V*.md filenames, or only the new Schedule Spec naming?
qAndA.answer: nah just spec, we'll depricate arc usage in name.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: Automatic discovery recognizes only Schedule Spec V*.md. Schedule Architecture naming is deprecated and is not an automatic input pattern; an explicit path may still be used if needed during transition.
Should the skill use a stable Weekly Schedule Sheet contract with dynamic task content, while stopping on unsupported changes to categories, day count, budget rules, or free-day model?

Self-resolved decision: Use a stable seven-day Weekly Schedule Sheet contract with dynamically derived task content and current POW/POF/Sleep accounting. Stop and flag unsupported structural changes instead of guessing.

Should the skill infer the free day from each Schedule Spec, or should Sunday remain a permanent rule? My recommendation is to infer the designated free day, show it in the sheet, exclude it from aggregates by default, and stop on unclear or unsupported free-day rules.
qAndA.answer: your recc works. but definelty make sure not to forget about the importance of leaving out free day accounting. I usually probably wont want that unless specifically stated that I want free day accounting.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: The skill will infer the designated free day from each Schedule Spec and display that day, but free-day accounting is excluded from weekly totals, averages, percentages, rankings, flex calculations, and other aggregates by default. Free-day accounting may be included only when the user explicitly requests it; the skill must not infer that request merely because the spec describes a free-day budget.
Should each daily schedule table use the columns #, Task, POF, POW, and Sleep, with dynamic rows, special-case markers, and longer instructions kept in an associated details section?

Self-resolved decision: Daily tables use the # / Task / POF / POW / Sleep layout. Step IDs remain task identity; each task is assigned to one category; Flex, Conditional, and NR are marked; detailed subtasks and instructions live in an associated details section.

Should the skill adopt a strict, versioned Schedule Spec contract feeding a normalized schedule model, deterministic validation, and deterministic Weekly Schedule Sheet rendering, while tolerating harmless formatting changes but never guessing about ambiguous meaning?
qAndA.answer: that sounds like a great idea yes.

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: The long-term implementation strategy is a strict, versioned Schedule Spec contract that feeds a normalized intermediate model, deterministic validation, and deterministic Weekly Schedule Sheet rendering. The skill may tolerate harmless Markdown formatting differences, but it must stop on ambiguous meaning; free-day accounting remains opt-in.

Should normal build-schedule-sheet operation require a canonical Schedule Spec, stop on prose-only input, provide an internal template, and keep legacy conversion as a separate explicit migration path?

Self-resolved decision: Normal build-schedule-sheet operation requires canonical Schedule Spec input. Prose-only or structurally incomplete documents stop before generation; the package includes a Schedule Spec template; legacy conversion is separate and explicit rather than hidden in the builder.

Should the canonical Schedule Spec use a strict JSON block inside Markdown, with format_version for schema evolution, content_version for the schedule version, and prose retained only as supporting context?

Self-resolved decision: Canonical Schedule Specs use a strict JSON block inside Markdown. The structured block is authoritative; format_version tracks schema evolution, content_version tracks the schedule version, and surrounding prose is supporting context only.
Should each Schedule Spec task require a stable explicit ID, separate from its display name and display order?

Self-resolved decision: Every Schedule Spec task requires a unique stable machine ID. The ID is distinct from the human-readable name and numeric display order; tasks are never merged solely because their names match.
Should the Schedule Spec use explicit day assignments as the source of truth and derive frequency from them?
qAndA.answer: we're starting to ask a lot of questions are you keep track of the decision tree?\nYour recc works

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: Explicit day assignments are authoritative; recurrence/frequency is derived from those assignments. Use a simple days array for ordinary tasks and explicit assignment records when a task has per-day duration differences or multiple occurrences on one day. The decision tree is being tracked internally, while every asked exchange and self-resolved decision is appended to the session JSON.
Should each Weekly Schedule Sheet include a concise provenance block with source spec, spec version, format version, builder name, and free-day accounting mode?

Self-resolved decision: Generated sheets include concise provenance metadata identifying the source spec, content/spec version, format version, build-schedule-sheet skill, and whether free-day accounting is excluded or explicitly included.
Should an existing output collision stop the workflow and require an explicit choice to use another destination, replace the existing sheet, or cancel, with no automatic overwrite?

Self-resolved decision: Existing Weekly Schedule Sheet collisions are blockers. The skill never overwrites automatically; it presents the collision and requires an explicit destination change, replacement approval, or cancellation.
Should the Schedule Spec store durations as integer minutes internally while the Weekly Schedule Sheet displays all durations and totals in human-readable hours-and-minutes notation?
qAndA.answer: yeah human readable h and minutes. and then internally you can calculate as minutes

qAndA.question: Self-resolved decision: Store and calculate all durations as integer minutes internally. Render human-readable h/m notation consistently in daily tables, totals, breakdowns, flex blocks, and task details; decimal-hour notation is not used in the generated sheet.

Self-resolved decision: The builder will require an explicit calendar model in the canonical Schedule Spec, including the seven named days and designated free day. If the free day is missing, invalid, or structurally incompatible, generation stops rather than assuming Sunday.

Self-resolved decision: A newer unsupported Schedule Spec format_version is a blocker. The skill may support known schema versions through explicit migrations, but it must not reinterpret an unknown schema silently.

Self-resolved decision: The package will include its own schedule-spec contract reference, weekly-schedule-sheet output contract reference, canonical Schedule Spec template, and deterministic parser/validator/renderer scripts. These are internal package resources and do not depend on the existing V5 document at runtime.

Self-resolved decision: Conditional tasks are visible in the Weekly Schedule Sheet and clearly marked. They do not contribute to fixed daily or weekly accounting by default; they contribute only when the user explicitly requests that conditional work be counted or the Schedule Spec explicitly marks it as required. NR tasks remain visible as recommendations with zero scheduled minutes and are excluded from totals, rankings, flex calculations, and percentages.

Self-resolved decision: Flex behavior is explicit, not inferred from task names. A task must be marked as a flex/remainder allocation in the Schedule Spec. The validator calculates remaining minutes only after required fixed assignments, excluding conditional and NR time; missing or ambiguous flex ownership is a blocker.

Self-resolved decision: Subtasks are execution details within a parent task by default and are not counted in addition to the parent. Independently scheduled subtasks require their own stable task IDs. A conflict between parent duration and explicit subtask allocation is a blocker.

Self-resolved decision: Source version metadata must be unambiguous. The builder uses the structured content_version and checks it against a version in the filename when both exist; disagreement, missing version metadata, or unsafe normalization is a blocker. The output preserves the version value in a lowercase filename.

Self-resolved decision: Deterministic scripts own parsing, normalization, validation, calculations, and rendering. Correctness-impacting findings block generation; non-blocking warnings are shown in the preflight and still require explicit approval before the final sheet is written.

Self-resolved decision: The generated sheet contains provenance and accounting rules, a legend, a master summary, ordered daily tables, category breakdowns, a task-to-day matrix, ranked weekly task hours, and an associated task-details/execution-notes section. Insight Highlights and Clarifying Q&A are not generated. The contract is semantic and stable; unsupported structural changes stop the workflow.

Self-resolved decision: The build-schedule-sheet trigger surface covers creating or generating a Weekly Schedule Sheet from a Schedule Spec. The skill is not for editing the Schedule Spec, general schedule planning, or silently converting legacy prose documents; those are separate tasks.

summary: The user wants a self-contained build-schedule-sheet skill that creates Weekly Schedule Sheets from canonical Schedule Spec Markdown documents. The primary scope is creating new sheets; updating an existing sheet is not a separate workflow. Input terminology is Schedule Spec; output terminology is Weekly Schedule Sheet; output filenames use lowercase weekly-schedule-sheet-v<content-version>.md and preserve the source version. Automatic discovery recognizes only Schedule Spec V*.md, while legacy architecture naming is deprecated and legacy prose conversion is a separate migration task. Normal operation requires a canonical Schedule Spec containing an authoritative JSON block inside Markdown, with format_version for schema evolution and content_version for schedule identity. Every task requires a stable unique ID separate from display name and order; explicit day assignments are authoritative and recurrence is derived. The skill uses a normalized intermediate model, deterministic validation, calculations, and rendering, and blocks ambiguous, contradictory, unsupported, or incomplete input rather than guessing. Durations are calculated internally as integer minutes and displayed as human-readable hours and minutes. The generated sheet is self-contained and does not depend on weekly-scheduleV5.md at runtime. Standard output includes provenance, legend, master summary, ordered daily tables, POW/POF/Sleep breakdowns, task-to-day matrix, ranked weekly task hours, and task details/execution notes; Insight Highlights and Clarifying Q&A are excluded. The designated free day is inferred and shown, but free-day accounting is excluded from aggregates by default and included only when explicitly requested. Generation creates a temporary draft and preflight, requires approval before writing, and never overwrites an existing output silently. The package follows write-a-skill-v2 and Karpathy protocols, with internal references, a Schedule Spec template, and deterministic scripts where useful.
